les: Sê dit so dat dit help
kaps_punt: Gee en ontvang terugvoering: gee terugvoering aan vriende en ontvang terugvoering van vriende en volwassenes

items.bewering: Van jou eie werk sien 'n mens nie altyd alles self nie.
items.blok: Wat is terugvoering?
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley feedback model, as summarised in Wisniewski et al., 'The Power of Feedback Revisited', Frontiers in Psychology 2020 (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.03087/full): feedback exists to close the gap between where the learner is and where they need to be, which the learner often cannot see alone

items.bewering: Wanneer iemand anders vir jou sê wat hy daarvan dink, kry jy terugvoering. Jy kry ook terugvoering oor iets wat jy gedoen het.
items.blok: Wat is terugvoering?
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley definition (feedback is information given by an agent about aspects of one's performance or understanding), via Wisniewski et al. 2020, Frontiers in Psychology; it covers performance and conduct, not only products

items.bewering: Terugvoering vertel jou watter deel al werk en watter deel nog nie.
items.blok: Wat is terugvoering?
items.bron: Federation University Australia, 'Types of feedback' (https://federation.edu.au/staff/learning-and-teaching/teaching-practice/feedback/types-of-feedback); Study.com summary of positive and negative student feedback: positive feedback marks what met the objective, negative feedback what has not yet

items.bewering: Positiewe terugvoering sê vir jou watter deel al klaar werk. Negatiewe terugvoering sê vir jou watter deel nog nie werk nie.
items.blok: Negatief beteken nie onvriendelik nie
items.bron: Study.com, 'Student Feedback Types' (https://study.com/learn/lesson/student-feedback-types-examples-positive.html): positive feedback when an objective is met, negative feedback on what has not been met and needs improvement

items.bewering: Albei soorte is terugvoering en albei kan vriendelik gesê word.
items.blok: Negatief beteken nie onvriendelik nie
items.bron: Kim Scott, Radical Candor, 'Praise in Public, Criticize in Private' (https://www.radicalcandor.com/blog/public-praise-private-criticism): criticism given with care and respect; 'negative' in feedback means corrective, not hostile (PMC10504910 on negative feedback in academic settings)

items.bewering: Jou maat wys sy plakkaat vir jou en jy sê net mooi. Hy weet nie watter deel hy volgende keer weer so moet doen nie. Sê eerder presies wat gewerk het.
items.blok: Sê presies wat goed was
items.bron: IRIS Center, Vanderbilt, 'Providing Positive Feedback' (https://iris.peabody.vanderbilt.edu/module/ecbm/cresource/q2/p06/): specific praise tells the child what to repeat, general praise does not; Hattie & Timperley: global praise is the least informative feedback

items.bewering: Sê dit vir hom self en nie net vir die kinders langs jou nie.
items.blok: Sê presies wat goed was
items.bron: Radical Candor, 'Praise in Public, Criticize in Private' (https://www.radicalcandor.com/blog/public-praise-private-criticism): praise should reach the person praised; nothing here conflicts with the later advice to give correction privately

items.bewering: Die woord sleg keur die hele werk af en wys geen deel uit nie.
items.blok: Praat oor die werk en nie oor die mens nie
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley via Wisniewski et al. 2020 and the BERA blog on their feedback levels (https://www.bera.ac.uk/blog/how-to-optimise-the-use-of-hattie-and-timperleys-feedback-levels-for-student-learning): a global verdict gives no information about which part to change

items.bewering: Die woorde oor mooi skryf gaan oor hom en nie oor sy werk nie.
items.blok: Praat oor die werk en nie oor die mens nie
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley: feedback about the self as a person is the least effective level, feedback about the task and process more effective (BERA blog; Family Medicine 2025, Lee, 'An Exploration of Feedback Using Hattie and Timperley's Feedback Levels')

items.bewering: Die tweede manier sê die letters onderaan is te klein. Dit sê ook vir hom om volgende keer groter te skryf.
items.blok: Praat oor die werk en nie oor die mens nie
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley 'where to next' (feed-forward) question, via Wisniewski et al. 2020, Frontiers in Psychology: effective feedback names the gap and the next step

items.bewering: Sê so iets liewer eenkant, waar die ander kinders nie hoor nie.
items.blok: Praat oor die werk en nie oor die mens nie
items.bron: Radical Candor, 'Praise in Public, Criticize in Private: Why It Works' (https://www.radicalcandor.com/blog/public-praise-private-criticism): criticism in front of peers causes embarrassment and defensiveness; the lesson's 'liewer' matches the rule-of-thumb status these sources give it

items.bewering: Kies ook die oomblik en wag as jou maat haastig is.
items.blok: Praat oor die werk en nie oor die mens nie
items.bron: Galileo Camps, 'Feedback How-Tos' (https://galileo-camps.com/blog/feedback-how-tos-how-to-give-it-take-it-and-help-your-kids-use-it/) and Kidpreneurs, 'Teaching Kids to Give and Receive Effective Feedback': timing is part of giving feedback well; advice, not a factual claim that can fail

items.bewering: Soms sê iemand vir jou wat jy goed gedoen het. Sê dankie daarvoor en moenie sê dit was niks nie.
items.blok: Wanneer iemand vir jou terugvoering gee
items.bron: SocialSelf, 'How to Accept Compliments' (https://socialself.com/blog/accept-compliments/) and On The Right Track, 'The Do's and Don'ts of Accepting Compliments': say thank you; avoid 'it was nothing', which dismisses the giver

items.bewering: Luister eers klaar voordat jy antwoord of jouself verduidelik. Sê daarna dankie vir sy moeite. Vra hom uit oor die deel wat jy nie verstaan nie.
items.blok: Wanneer iemand vir jou terugvoering gee
items.bron: Galileo Camps, 'Feedback How-Tos' and Kidpreneurs, 'Teaching Kids to Give and Receive Effective Feedback' (https://kidpreneurs.org/teaching-kids-to-give-and-receive-effective-feedback/): listen without interrupting, thank the giver, ask questions to clarify

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie dadelik saam te stem nie, en jy mag eers daaroor gaan dink.
items.blok: Wanneer iemand vir jou terugvoering gee
items.bron: Galileo Camps, 'Feedback How-Tos': listen to understand, then take thinking time before deciding; no source requires immediate agreement

items.bewering: Dieselfde geld vir 'n grootmens, soos jou onderwyser of jou ouma. Jou ouma sê dalk iets oor hoe jy gehelp het.
items.blok: Wanneer iemand vir jou terugvoering gee
items.bron: Same sources as the preceding receiving-feedback items; the advice applies by source irrespective of who gives the feedback. Checked for child safety: extending 'jy hoef nie dadelik saam te stem nie' to adults teaches no obligation to comply

items.bewering: Die rooi merke op jou somme is terugvoering en nie straf nie.
items.blok: Wanneer iemand vir jou terugvoering gee
items.bron: Marking as feedback: Hattie & Timperley via Wisniewski et al. 2020. Red pen: Laerskool Nelspruit, Akademiese Beleid Intermediêre- en Seniorfase (laerskoolnelspruit.co.za, 2022), which has learners write in blue and teachers mark in red, a South African school policy. Colour is incidental to the claim

items.bewering: Party woorde breek 'n mens af en is nie terugvoering nie. Iemand lag jou uit of noem jou lelike name. Sulke woorde sê niks oor jou werk of jou daad nie en help jou nie.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley definition (feedback is information about performance): ridicule and name-calling carry no information about the work; McMillen Health, 'Words Hurt: Verbal Bullying' (https://www.mcmillenhealth.org/tamtalks/verbal-bullying) classes name-calling and mocking as verbal aggression

items.bewering: Hulle maak jou seer, ook as die mens sê hy het net 'n grap gemaak.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: Understood.org, 'The difference between teasing and bullying' (https://www.understood.org/en/articles/difference-between-teasing-and-bullying); Scholastic, 'When Teasing Becomes Bullying': how a 'joke' is received matters more than the teller's stated intent

items.bewering: Sulke woorde kan afknouery wees. Woorde oor jou werk kan ook afknouery wees, as ander kinders jou daarmee oor en oor afbreek.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: StopBullying.gov, 'What Is Bullying' (https://www.stopbullying.gov/bullying/what-is-bullying): verbal attacks are bullying when repeated or likely to be repeated and there is a power imbalance. 'kan' correctly avoids saying every insult is bullying. 'afknouery' is established South African Afrikaans for bullying (skole.co.za, 'Oorsake van afknouery in skole'; AfriForum Teenboelie)

items.bewering: Sê dit vir 'n grootmens wat jy vertrou. Dit kan die grootmens by die huis wees, jou onderwyser, die skoolhoof of 'n ander grootmens in die familie.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: Department of Basic Education, 'Addressing bullying in the schooling environment' (https://www.education.gov.za/ArchivedDocuments/ArchivedArticles/Addressingbullyingintheschoolingenvironment.aspx): learners report to teachers or the School Management Team, and to parents or any trustworthy adult; KidsHealth, 'Dealing With Bullies (for Kids)' (https://kidshealth.org/en/kids/bullies.html): teachers, principals and parents can stop bullying. Help-route check: every adult named can act, and the route does not depend on the bully. No outside line such as Childline is named, but that leaves nothing untrue

items.bewering: As die eerste een nie luister nie, sê dit vir die volgende een. Hou aan sê totdat iemand iets daaraan doen.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: KidsHealth, 'Dealing With Bullying' (https://kidshealth.org/en/teens/bullies.html): 'tell someone about it and keep telling until something is done'; PACER Teens Against Bullying, 'Tell an Adult': if the first person cannot help, reach out to another trusted adult

items.bewering: Om dit te stop, is die grootmense se werk en nie joune nie.
items.blok: Wanneer woorde nie meer terugvoering is nie
items.bron: StopBullying.gov, 'Respond to Bullying' and 'Support the Children Involved' (https://www.stopbullying.gov/prevention/support-the-children-involved): adults stop bullying and kids should not handle it alone; DBE (above) puts the response with teachers and the School Management Team. Child-responsibility check: nowhere in the lesson is the child made responsible for another person's behaviour. Block 4 asks the child only to govern their own way of giving feedback

items.bewering: terugvoering: Wanneer iemand sê wat aan jou werk of jou daad goed is of wat nie.
items.blok: terugvoering
items.bron: Hattie & Timperley definition via Wisniewski et al. 2020. Read alone, it agrees with the lesson's use: it covers work and deeds (the ouma's comment, the red marks), and it excludes remarks about the person, which is the lesson's own point in block 4. Ridicule and name-calling say nothing about the work, so they do not fit it, as block 6 says. It does not settle whether repeated put-downs about the work are still feedback, but the lesson calls them 'kan ook afknouery wees' without saying they are not feedback, so the two do not contradict

items.bewering: positiewe terugvoering: Terugvoering wat sê watter deel van jou werk of jou daad al klaar werk.
items.blok: positiewe terugvoering
items.bron: Study.com, 'Student Feedback Types'; Federation University, 'Types of feedback'. Read alone, it matches the sentence in block 2 almost word for word and does not imply 'friendly'

items.bewering: negatiewe terugvoering: Terugvoering wat sê watter deel van jou werk of jou daad nog nie werk nie.
items.blok: negatiewe terugvoering
items.bron: Study.com, 'Student Feedback Types' (negative feedback addresses what has not been met and needs improvement). Read alone, it agrees with block 2 and, correctly, carries no connotation of unkindness

items.bewering: afknouery: Aspris seermaak wat oor en oor gebeur, deur 'n ander kind of 'n groep kinders met meer mag.
items.blok: afknouery
items.bron: StopBullying.gov, 'What Is Bullying' (aggressive behaviour among school-aged children, a real or perceived power imbalance, repetition); DBE, 'Addressing bullying in the schooling environment' ('deliberately hurting'); Olweus's classic definition requires repetition over time. Read alone, it agrees with the lesson's use: block 6 says 'kan' of one-off insults and 'oor en oor' of repeated put-downs by 'ander kinders'. Note: StopBullying.gov also counts behaviour that is 'likely to be repeated', so 'oor en oor gebeur' is the narrower Olweus form. That is defensible, and the lesson tells the child to report either way

opsomming: All 27 checkable claims were checked afresh against sources and every one holds: the lesson contains no superlatives and no analogy blocks, each of the four glossary entries read alone agrees with how the lesson uses the word, no sentence makes a child responsible for anyone else's behaviour, and the help route (a trusted adult at home, the teacher, the principal or family, and keep telling until someone acts) matches the Department of Basic Education's reporting guidance and would work, though it names no outside line such as Childline.
